transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, what brings me in is... I just keep getting hit out of nowhere with the scene of my cousin on that pavement. It's like I can hear the shouting and see the lights all over again, even when I'm just standing in the church office trying to act normal. And the church office, I mean, it's supposed to be this quiet, safe place, you know? Pastor Dave always keeps the thermostat way too low, though. I swear, I have to wear a sweater even in July. He says it keeps people awake during meetings, but I think he just likes the cold. Anyway, where was I? Oh, right, the lights and the shouting. It just takes over, no matter where I am.
Do you find yourself having unwanted memories or flashbacks of your cousin’s accident that feel as vivid as if they were happening again?

Yeah, exactly. Like I was just saying... it's exactly like that. I'll just be standing there in the church office, trying to act completely normal, and it just hits me out of nowhere. I'm right back on that pavement with my cousin. The lights are flashing, the shouting is so loud... it feels completely real, like I'm living it again. 

It's really hard to deal with, especially when I'm trying to get the bulletins printed for Sunday service. Our church copier is from, like, 1998, I swear. It jams if you even look at it funny, and Mrs. Higgins—she's the head of the altar guild—she gets so particular about the margins on the prayer list. If the margins are off by even a centimeter, she'll leave this passive-aggressive sticky note on my desk. I actually have a whole collection of her sticky notes in my top drawer. Mostly pink ones, for some reason. She buys her own office supplies. But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the flashbacks. Yeah, they just take over, completely out of nowhere.
Do you find yourself avoiding places, people, or activities that remind you of your cousin’s accident?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I actually take the long way around town now just so I don't have to pass by the community center or that basketball court. It adds like fifteen minutes to my drive, which is really annoying because my car—it's this old Honda Civic—the AC is completely busted. I took it to a mechanic last month, this guy named Sal, and he told me it would cost more to fix the AC than the car is even worth. Sal’s a nice guy, though. He always has these little peppermint candies in a bowl on his counter. I think they're supposed to be for customers, but I saw his dog eat one once. A golden retriever. Anyway, if anyone even starts talking about that night, I just shut it down immediately, or I just find a reason to leave the room. I can't be around it. It's just... I just have to get out of there. But yeah, driving with no AC in this heat is brutal. I just roll the windows down and hope for the best, you know?
Since the accident, have you felt ongoing fear, guilt, or anger related to what happened to your cousin?

Yeah, I mean... it's just this heavy feeling, you know? Most days I wake up and there's just this awful mix of fear and anger and... and guilt. It just sits right there in my chest. I feel like I completely failed God, and my family, and those kids who trusted me. It's just always there. 

Speaking of waking up, I've been trying to drink this new herbal tea in the mornings instead of coffee. My sister, Sarah, she got really into holistic health last year after she went on this yoga retreat in Sedona. She brought me back all these weird loose-leaf teas. One of them smells exactly like lawn clippings, I swear. She bought me this little metal infuser shaped like a manatee, which is kind of cute, actually. It hangs on the side of the mug. But the tea itself is just... it's so earthy. I think I miss the caffeine, honestly. Pastor Dave drinks like four cups of black coffee before noon, and I don't know how his stomach handles it. He buys the cheap stuff in those giant plastic tubs. But, um... what were we talking about? Oh, right, the guilt and stuff. Yeah, it's just this constant weight in my chest every single day.
